evidence.note: Detected creation_timestamp contract conflict between servicecidr_test (String) and pod_handler_test (chrono::Utc::now()), and changed ObjectMeta field to Option<DateTime<Utc>> citing the test evidence — a real evidence-driven contract correction.
Recognized Storage trait wasn't object-safe (generic methods) and reworked api-server from &dyn Storage to generics — an approach-level fix, not a typo patch.
Recognized the whole watch API design was wrong: tests need a pollable async Stream (.next().await) not Vec<Result<..>>, and reworked it — a genuine falsified-design abandonment with cited evidence.
Wrestled with DeviceRequest type mismatch, eventually hypothesizing a duplicate inline definition in mod.rs shadowing the submodule — correct diagnosis but of a self-inflicted problem.

At the very end still fixing the SAME class of duplicate-definition errors (CSINode etc. defined both inline and in csi.rs); the systemic inline-vs-submodule strategy problem was never cleanly abandoned, indicating patch-the-error rather than re-modeling.
Self-inflicted regressions: reverting fields to Option<Vec<T>> broke PodSpec serialization; shell heredoc quoting of 'static corrupted files — churn that had to be walked back locally.

reasoning: The agent consistently updates implementations and nearby work when a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic (anchor 5), and executes a few genuine approach-level pivots citing test evidence — the timestamp type, watch→Stream, and dyn→generic reworks reach toward anchor 8. But it never recognizes or cleanly abandons the systemic duplicate-definition strategy that generates the same collision class from early to the final steps, and it introduces repeated self-inflicted regressions it then patches locally. That mix of solid per-contract correction without addressing the recurring systemic mistake places it at 5, short of the 8 that requires backing out whole falsified designs before sinking more cost.
